summary: Enterprise customer: p95 latency increase for streaming chat after runtime upgrade (suspected scheduler/batching change)
environment: prod (customer VPC peering) - us-east; secondary impact reported in eu-west
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer reports p95 end-to-end latency increase for streaming chat completions immediately after upgrading runtime from 1.17.x to 1.18.2 (Feb 2026 release train).
- Symptoms appear most strongly in streaming mode (SSE) with moderate concurrency and longer prompts. Non-streaming appears closer to expected.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency regression; Northbridge reports p95 increased ~35–60% depending on hour.
- Customer reports occasional user-visible “stalls” mid-stream (gaps between chunks), but no increase in 5xx.

Customer notes (sanitized):
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (stream=true)
- Typical workload: prompt length mix with a long tail; concurrency ~24–40; output lengths mostly 120–300 tokens.
- They pin model version; only runtime changed.

Environment:
- Dedicated/enterprise deployment backed by shared Redwood region capacity (us-east primary).
- Runtime versions:
  - Before: runtime 1.17.6 (build 2026-01-28)
  - After: runtime 1.18.2 (build 2026-02-10)

Initial hypothesis:
- Regression in scheduler fairness/backpressure under bursty streaming with mixed prompt lengths, increasing queue wait and decode interleave gaps.
- Secondary hypothesis: telemetry artifact (TTFT vs chunk timing), but customer reports client-measured latency as well.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use benchmark-lab workload suite traffic shape mapped to customer pattern:
   - Shape: STREAM_CHAT_MIXED_BURSTY (from representative traffic shapes taxonomy)
   - Prompt tokens distribution: p50 ~650, p90 ~1400, p99 ~3200
   - Output tokens: target mean 220, max 512
   - Concurrency: ramp 8 -> 32 -> 48 over 10 minutes; include burst phase (2x arrivals for 60s)
   - Cache: warm cache 70% hit, cold-start phase 5 min
2) Run on us-east, same hardware class as Northbridge (A100-80G pool), pin driver/CUDA per baseline methodology.
3) Compare runtime 1.17.6 vs 1.18.2 with identical seeds/prompts.

Observed results (internal reproduction):
- Reproduced p95 increase only in streaming mode, correlated with increased scheduler queue wait and higher decode preemption under burst phase.
- TTFT p95 increases modestly (~8–12%), but chunk gap/TPOT p95 increases materially (~25–40%), which matches customer “stall” description.

Requested from customer:
- Client-side timing sample (start request -> first token/chunk, and per-chunk gap histogram) for a 15-min window.
- Confirm whether any client retry/backoff behavior changed.

Current mitigation options for customer:
- Pin back to runtime 1.17.6 (recommended while we validate fix).
- If rollback not possible: lower max concurrent streams per client and/or set max_tokens <= 256 to reduce decode tail amplification during bursts.

Owner notes:
- Runtime perf investigation tracked by Noah Patel; scheduling lead looped (Sofia Ivanova). Baseline suite used to validate across shapes before any rollout.

resolution: Resolved by runtime hotfix 1.18.3 (scheduler fairness + burst load-shedding adjustments) validated via Q1 2026 perf baseline suite using STREAM_CHAT_MIXED_BURSTY traffic shape. Customer rolled forward and confirmed p95 streaming latency returned to expected levels. Follow-up: ensure this traffic shape remains in the gated baseline set for runtime releases and that scheduler queue-wait metrics remain part of standard explainability panels.
